items.title: Michael Max Fleming interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, June 8, 2017
items.q: I come up off of a break one night and there’s this guy sitting there, an older gentleman. His name was Ben Webster. So I come up to him, “Good evening, sir.”

ctx.x: What happens as a bassist when you go to play a gig and maybe it’s a pick-up group or something, and someone calls a tune and you don’t know it. But you’re supposed to know it. You’re supposed to be responsible for outlining the changes. How do you get through that?

I got through that from one big experience from — I didn’t tell you but the first major gig that I got in after I moved to New York was with Mary Lou Williams — the liaison between the swing and the bebop. A lot of people don’t know it but she helped Monk form his sound, helped Bud Powell form their sounds. She was well respected. She’s my musical mother, and that’s within the first six weeks I got into her hands and her influence. So she’s coming out of retirement, she’s playing at Wells. Upstairs they had two…
